title: Green synthesis and metal-dependent bioactivity of resveratrol hemisuccinate Zn( ii ) and Cu( ii ) complexes
content: Resveratrol (trans-3,4′,5-trihydroxystilbene) is a naturally occurring stilbenoid known for its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer activities. However, its large-scale production from natural sources is constrained by low yields and costly extraction processes. Moreover, its therapeutic use is limited by poor aqueous solubility and low bioavailability. In this study, a green and sustainable strategy is developed for the synthesis of resveratrol via a decarbonylative Heck coupling reaction. This approach enables efficient construction of the stilbene framework through carbon–carbon bond formation using cobalt nanoparticles supported on carbon nanotubes as an environmentally friendly alternative to traditional palladium-based catalysts. Subsequently, resveratrol is functionalized to afford resveratrol hemisuccinate, which is further complexed with biologically relevant Zn(ii) and Cu(ii) to enhance its biological performance. The resulting metal complexes are expected to influence the cellular redox balance through reactive oxygen species (ROS), which may contribute to improved anticancer activity. The synthesized compounds were evaluated using complementary computational (in silico) and experimental (in vitro) approaches to better understand their biological activity and structure–activity relationships. Overall, this work presents a sustainable synthetic route to resveratrol and demonstrates the potential of resveratrol hemisuccinate-bases Zn(ii) and Cu(ii) complexes as promising candidates for future therapeutic applications.
